bib.title: Decomposed Prompting: A Modular Approach for Solving Complex Tasks

read.skipped: Appendix G (task prompts, text lines ~1600-3990) read in part: the letter-concatenation prompts in full, the rest (CommaQA, open-domain QA, math prompts with long context passages) skimmed from the tail and spot checks only.

question: Can a complex task be solved better with few-shot LLMs by decomposing it into sub-tasks, each handled by its own prompt, further decomposition or symbolic function, than by one chain-of-thought prompt?
hypothesis: Separate, modular sub-task prompts teach hard sub-tasks better than a single CoT prompt, and allow recursion and symbolic modules (retrieval) to be plugged in.
contributions: Decomposed Prompting (DecomP): a decomposer prompt writes a sequence of (sub-task, sub-question) steps, each routed to a sub-task handler (few-shot prompt, further decomposer, or symbolic function)
Shows hierarchical decomposition (kth letter), recursive decomposition (list reversal), external API calls (Elasticsearch retrieval), and error-correcting post-processing of CoT (math QA)
Outperforms CoT and least-to-most prompting on four case studies with GPT-3 models

method.summary: A decomposer LLM prompt is called iteratively; given the question and history of sub-answers it emits the next sub-question tagged with a handler name in square brackets, until it emits [EOQ]. A symbolic controller routes each sub-question to the handler (a separate few-shot prompt, another decomposer, or a retriever), appends the answer (#i references) to the decomposer history, and handles operators such as foreach. Compared against CoT, CoT with rollout and least-to-most with rollout on four tasks, plus a math post-processing study.
method.task: multi-step reasoning by prompt decomposition: kth-letter concatenation, list reversal, long-context multi-hop QA (CommaQA-E), open-domain multi-hop QA, math QA answer extraction

datasets.name: kth letter concatenation (k=3, space or semicolon delimiter)
datasets.size: 100 examples per evaluation dataset, 4 datasets (new k=3; 4 and 5 words; new delimiter ';')
datasets.split: N=3 IID, N=4 and 5 OOD words; prompts show k=1, 4, last on 3-word strings
datasets.source: words from most popular first and last names (forebears.io)

datasets.name: list reversal
datasets.split: prompts have 3 examples of 3-5 items; test on 4, 6, 8, 10 items
datasets.source: vocabulary from Wei et al. 2022 (vocabulary.com list 189583)

datasets.name: CommaQA-E (reduced version)
datasets.source: Khot et al. 2022; synthetic entities, facts, multi-hop questions
datasets.preprocessing: smaller regenerated version so at least four examples fit in CoT context (GPT-3 limit 2049 tokens)

datasets.name: 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, HotpotQA (open-domain)
datasets.size: 300 held-out dev questions each; 20 annotated train questions for prompts; 100 held-out questions for tuning K
datasets.split: 3 prompts of 15 questions each sampled from the 20
datasets.source: HotpotQA fullwiki corpus; 2Wiki corpus 430,225 paragraphs and MuSiQue 139,416 paragraphs built by pooling paragraphs of train, dev and test questions
datasets.preprocessing: 2Wiki and MuSiQue converted from reading comprehension to open-domain via pooled corpora

other.use: default LLM for letter concatenation, CommaQA, math, and all decomposers
open-domain QA sub-task QA models; decomposition still done by GPT3-sized models because only those reliably produce the structured output

inference.samples: 3 different prompts (example sets) per method, averaged, for letter concatenation, CommaQA and open-domain QA; single run per prompt; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: few-shot; decomposer prompt plus one few-shot prompt per sub-task handler. Letter task: prompts show k=1, 4, last on 3-word strings. CommaQA: each sub-task prompt has 8 QA examples (2 questions per paragraph). Open-domain: 15 questions per prompt. CoT baselines are run in the same decomposition framework with a regex answer extractor ('.* outputs "(.*)"\.').
inference.retrieval: Elasticsearch; K paragraphs retrieved per retrieval round; K chosen by grid search on 100 held-out questions per dataset: NoDecomp-Ctxt K in {6,8,10} for GPT3 and {2,4,6,8} for Flan-T5; Decomp-Ctxt K in {2,4,6} for both. Retrieval index/BM25 settings not stated.

parameters.operators: select (default, substitutes #i answers); project_values (foreach: one question per list element, answers concatenated); project_values_flat_unique (foreach_merge: also flattens and keeps unique entities)
parameters.recursion: list reversal splits list in halves (O(log n) calls), base case lists of length 3 solved by CoT; tail-split variant is O(n) calls

metrics.name: Exact Match (EM)
metrics.definition: exact string match; set equality for order-independent list answers

metrics.name: Answer F1
metrics.definition: prediction and ground truth treated as bags of tokens, precision and recall (Rajpurkar et al. 2016)

baselines: CoT w/ rollout (decomposition procedure written as one CoT)
NoDecomp-Ctxt QA (single retrieval with the multi-hop question, K paragraphs)
eval.protocol: Average over 3 prompt sets for most tasks (following Perez et al. 2021); std dev reported in places, zero for DecomP on letter task; no significance test; per-prompt results in App. D.

availability.data: Datasets, code and prompts at the same repo; all prompts in supplementary material

prompts.purpose: decomposer prompt for kth letter concatenation
prompts.text:
QC: Take the letters at position 1 of the words in "Alan Mathison Turing" and concatenate them using a space.
QS: [split] What are the words in "Alan Mathison Turing"?
A: ["Alan", "Mathison", "Turing"]
QS: (project_values) [str_position] What is the letter at position 1 in "#1"?
A: ["A", "M", "T"]
QS: [merge] Concatenate #2 using a space.
A: "A M T"
QS: [EOQ]

prompts.purpose: answer extraction after CoT for math QA
prompts.text:
QC: There are 15 trees in the grove. ... How many trees did the grove workers plant today?
QS: [cot] <question>
A: <chain of thought>
QS: [gpt_ans] <chain of thought>
A: 6
QS: [EOQ]

results.setup: code-davinci-002, direct QA prompts, Elasticsearch retrieval; K tuned on 100 held-out questions

results.claim: With Flan-T5-XXL (11B) Decomp-Ctxt reaches 63.3 F1 on 2WikiMultihopQA, near Codex.

results.note: HotpotQA 56.4 vs 49.0 NoDecomp vs 24.8 No-Ctxt; MuSiQue 29.3 vs 23.3 vs 15.1.

results.claim: Replacing the regex answer extractor after CoT with a GPT-3 sub-task handler gains 14-17 pts on math QA.
results.setup: text-davinci-002, Wei et al. 2022 CoT prompts, answer extraction by GPT-3 handler (gpt_ans) instead of 'answer is' pattern
results.quote: resulting in a surprisingly high improvement of 14-17 pts
results.note: Text Sec 4.5 says GSM8K 36 -> 50.6; Fig 16 prints 36.0 and 50.7. MultiArith 78.0 -> 95.0.

results.claim: A single DecomP prompt set gives similar scores for the loop and generate decompositions of letter concatenation; tail-split list reversal is more stable at long lengths but needs O(n) calls versus O(log n) for halves.
results.quote: On the letter concatenation task, the results were exactly the same.

results.claim: Errors of DecomP on letter concatenation were only in sub-task execution (wrong letter extraction or concatenation), not in the decomposition.
results.quote: only found errors in the sub-task execution

limits: Decomposition and sub-task prompts are hand-written by the authors for each task; no automatic decomposition and no measure of the human effort.
Only GPT-3 era models (davinci, curie, Codex) and Flan-T5; Flan-T5 cannot produce the structured decomposition so GPT3-sized models are still needed as decomposer.
Baselines are CoT variants and least-to-most; the paper does not compare against each task-specific decomposition system.
Tasks are partly synthetic (letter concatenation, reversal, CommaQA); evaluation sets small (100 examples for letters, 300 for open-domain QA, 200-300 for math subsets).
No temperature, max tokens, retriever settings or seeds are reported; results are means over 3 prompt choices.
Cost and latency of the many sequential calls are not reported; the paper notes tail-split reversal needs O(n) calls versus O(log n).

terms.definition: the prompt that only describes the sequence of sub-tasks needed to solve the complex task
a few-shot prompted LLM, further decomposed prompt, or symbolic/learned function that implements one sub-task
project_values and project_values_flat_unique operators that iterate a sub-question over a list answer and (for merge) flatten and keep unique entities

lineage.note: main baseline; DecomP reuses its CoT prompts for reversal and math
closest work; DecomP differs by iterative top-down decomposition and non-linear structures
inspiration: decomposition in the language of existing agents; replaces supervised next-question generator with few-shot LLMs
